digest.component_or_area: MCP server error surface and CLI/library error code vocabulary
propositions: MCP tool failures currently surface only as prose in exception text; they must carry the same structured error discriminator (error_code) that the CLI already emits via error_envelope.

The CLI emits error codes from multiple sites (reads_cli, claim, transition, etc.) but these are bare string literals without a centralized vocabulary or registry; no single source of truth exists that spans CLI, library, and MCP interfaces.

MCP has two ad-hoc partial error shapes (_mcp_reads.py explain_criterion {error,kind} and _mcp_llm.py {error,...}) that diverge from the CLI's error_envelope and must be unified under a single error_code drawn from a shared classifier.

The library interface currently exposes no machine error discriminator; error_code_for(exc)->str and re-export of KNOWN_ERROR_CODES enables the library to participate in a cross-interface test verifying identical codes (ticket_not_found, concurrency_conflict, etc.) across CLI, library, and MCP.

TicketNotFoundError must be a distinct exception subclass raised only at the genuine not-found sites (reads.py:310/313) so isinstance-based classification yields message-independent error codes; message-keyed fallback (reads_cli.py:410) is left unchanged for AC6 CLI byte-parity.

The error_envelope schema currently requires input, but MCP failures without a target (gate refusal) have no input to resolve; relaxing error_envelope.required to [error,message] satisfies both conditional AC1 and schema, with CLI envelopes always populating input remaining valid.
